title: THE JUDGE WHO SOLD TOMORROW
deck: Chief magistrate Varo Pell built a painless temporal vault so no untried person would suffer a conscious day in prison. Then he sold the court's mornings to the wealthy, leaving 3,800 poor defendants suspended while years passed outside. When a cooling failure gives the vault nine hours, Illuminara must save every life without turning mass release into another way of refusing to hear the people at risk.
shape: Seven scenes across nine hours: a failing temporal vault beneath the court; the awakening of the woman whose case waited longest; discovery of a paid hearing calendar hidden inside a humane machine; a victim who refuses both blanket release and endless suspension; Pell's choice to open the ledger that can expose him; thirty-eight public review tables working while Illuminara and engineers stabilize the vault; and a dawn in which no one dies, most defendants regain proportionate freedom, dangerous cases receive real hearings, and the man who sold tomorrow begins to account for the time he took.

scenes.title: Nine Hours Under the Court
paragraphs: *Central Court of Lyr, temporal vault · 00:17, nine hours remaining*
The first sign of failure was not an alarm. It was rain.

Cold water gathered on the copper ribs of the temporal vault and fell through the blue light in slow, shining drops. Each drop crossed a suspension field and became a row of tiny spheres, nine versions of the same water occupying nine adjacent instants.
Thirty-eight hundred glass chambers descended beneath the court in twelve circular galleries. A person rested inside each one, painless and unaging while the city moved on without them.

Illuminara stood on the central bridge with one hand against a coolant trunk. The metal had split behind the wall. She could feel the fracture branching toward three more lines and the hot temporal coils pulling against ordinary time.
Vault engineer Ishan Rho knelt at an open service panel. His gloves smoked where he changed a valve.

**Ishan Rho**  
The reserve loop gives us nine hours if nothing else ruptures. If the core warms beyond eleven degrees, every chamber returns its occupant at a different fraction of a second.

**Illuminara**  
Alive?
Rho looked down through twelve galleries of sleeping faces.

**Ishan Rho**  
Some. The rest would arrive in pieces of time.
Chief magistrate Varo Pell came across the bridge without a coat. He was sixty, neat even at midnight, and carried the brass hearing seal that could open any chamber after a lawful order.

**Varo Pell**  
No chamber opens without review.

**Illuminara**  
Then begin the reviews.

**Varo Pell**  
There are three thousand eight hundred.

**Illuminara**  
There are nine hours.
Pell watched one suspended man whose hands were curled as though still holding the railing from which court guards had taken him.

**Varo Pell**  
Before this vault, untried people were beaten, sickened and recruited before any verdict. Here they feel no cold morning or frightened night.

**Illuminara**  
And no birthday.
His eyes sharpened, but he did not look away.

**Varo Pell**  
Open every chamber and some of these people will kill before breakfast. You will have saved their years by spending someone else's life.
The objection was not an excuse. That made the excuse around it more dangerous.
Illuminara followed the crack through the coolant rhythm. She could hold the metal, but no touch could make a judicial decision.

**Illuminara**  
I can give Rho a stable pressure while he builds a bypass. That protects the chance to decide. It does not decide for us.

**Illuminara**  
The people inside. The people who may be endangered outside. The clerks who know why hearings stopped. You. And the first person whose time this court took.
Pell's fingers closed around the hearing seal.

**Varo Pell**  
The oldest case is not the safest case.

**Illuminara**  
No. It is the first account we owe.
Another pipe gave a soft metallic cry. Illuminara pressed the fracture closed without crushing it.
The rain stopped. The clock did not.

scenes.title: The First Person Back
paragraphs: *Temporal vault, Gallery Twelve · 00:51, eight hours twenty-six minutes remaining*
The oldest occupied chamber belonged to Lysa Ansel.

Her record said thirty-two years old, municipal bookkeeper, accused of diverting winter fuel credits. The evidence packet had been complete for twelve years. Seven hearing dates had been cancelled. Beside the final cancellation, someone had entered a code that meant calendar displaced by priority petition.
Pell authorized the opening only after Ishan fitted a portable return cradle around the chamber.
Blue light folded inward. Lysa inhaled the last breath of a winter afternoon and exhaled into a summer midnight twelve years later.
Her first movement was to pull her sleeves over her hands. Her second was to search for a window.

**Lysa Ansel**  
The hearing room?

**Illuminara**  
Below it. You are safe. Your body has experienced less than a minute since arrest.
Lysa studied Illuminara's face, then Pell's seal.

**Lysa Ansel**  
How late are they?
Pell began to answer. Illuminara raised one finger, not to silence him but to keep his office from owning the first fact.

**Illuminara**  
Twelve years, eight months and four days have passed.
Lysa did not gasp. Her body had not yet learned enough of the new room to perform grief.

**Lysa Ansel**  
My son was six.

**Varo Pell**  
Your family was notified of every continuance.
Lysa looked at him as if he had answered a different question.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Was he six when he read them?
No one spoke.
Illuminara knew the public records, but those facts belonged to Lysa and not all at once.

**Illuminara**  
He is alive. He is eighteen. Would you like his current name and contact, or would you like someone you know to tell you?
Lysa pressed both palms against the return cradle.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Current name?

**Illuminara**  
He uses Ansel. He kept yours.
The first tear arrived before Lysa's face changed.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Then tell me why I am still accused.
A distributor had used Lysa's key while cameras placed her elsewhere. Its owner confessed eleven years ago; no prosecutor opposed dismissal.

**Varo Pell**  
This should have been closed.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Should have is a room with no door.
She touched the glass that had held her.

**Lysa Ansel**  
How many?

**Illuminara**  
Thirty-eight hundred chambers. Two hundred forty files are marked ready for immediate review. We believe many more contain enough evidence for a safe decision.

**Lysa Ansel**  
And the cooling?

**Ishan Rho**  
Eight hours now.
Lysa's legs trembled when she stood. Illuminara offered her forearm. Lysa took it, not because she trusted the court, but because the floor had acquired twelve years without asking her.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Do not make me the story that proves all of them are harmless.

**Illuminara**  
I won't.

**Lysa Ansel**  
And do not use one dangerous file to put me back.

**Illuminara**  
I won't do that either.
Lysa nodded once.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Then let me see the calendar that decided my son could grow up first.

scenes.title: The Market of Morning
paragraphs: *Central Court, sealed scheduling office · 01:39, seven hours thirty-eight minutes remaining*
Senior clerk Nemi Daro had slept in the scheduling office for three years.
A narrow cot stood between shelves of paper continuances. Nemi said the digital calendar could be altered, but paper still remembered pressure.
She placed two ledgers on the table. The public book listed hearing dates. The private one listed contributions to the Temporal Mercy Fund.

**Nemi Daro**  
Families funding expansion first received one priority hearing per chamber. Soon wealth bought Tuesday before poverty reached Monday.
Lysa turned pages. Each gold mark represented money received. Each black mark represented a hearing moved.

Illuminara laid the public calendar beside the private book. To every other eye, the black marks were cancellations. To hers, they were a rhythm: hundreds clustered in the forty-eight hours before quarterly Mercy Fund reports.
The same three lower-corner initials recurred. Cases moved just before the council counted fee income as proof that the vault could fund itself.

**Illuminara**  
The market did not merely buy mornings. It needed poor defendants to remain below so the fund could look indispensable.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Seven black marks beside my name.

**Varo Pell**  
The fees built twenty-six hundred chambers. Otherwise thousands stayed in prison.

**Nemi Daro**  
The old prison was closed in year four.

**Varo Pell**  
And the treasury refused full funding in year five.
Pell had built the first chambers after three innocent people died in a fevered remand block. Every later compromise had entered through that memory wearing the face of rescue.
Nemi opened a maintenance appendix. For six years, priority contributions had exceeded vault costs. The surplus financed a new court wing and reduced the justice levy.

**Varo Pell**  
End the petitions, and the council would reclaim the surplus and cut the vault. They loved painless detention because someone else paid.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Someone else did pay.
She put her palm on the private ledger.

**Lysa Ansel**  
We paid in time you could not see us feeling.
A tremor passed through the floor. Far below, Illuminara's field flexed around the coolant trunk.

**Ishan Rho, on comms**  
The fracture has reached Line Four. I can isolate it, but the old bypass drawings are wrong.
Pell looked toward the locked cabinet behind his desk.
Illuminara noticed.

**Illuminara**  
What is in there?

**Varo Pell**  
My working ledger.

**Nemi Daro**  
The true continuance reasons. Which petition displaced which case. Which files were ready. Which risk reports were current.

**Illuminara**  
You preserved a second answer. Why keep it if you meant the public never to hear it?

**Varo Pell**  
Because destroying it would have made the lie final.

**Varo Pell**  
It names every official involved. Open it, and half the people needed for reviews will protect themselves first.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Keep it closed and they spend our hours protecting you.
Pell placed the brass seal on the table but kept the cabinet key in his pocket.

**Varo Pell**  
You want a clean villain because a failed machine is easier to repair than a city that asked for mercy without paying for justice.

**Illuminara**  
I do not think you are clean.

**Illuminara**  
Understanding how you arrived does not erase where you arrived. Before I ask for the ledger again, we will hear the person whose danger you fear most.
Pell's hand left the key, but not his pocket.

scenes.title: The Person Outside the Chamber
paragraphs: *Central Court, Hearing Room One · 02:28, six hours forty-nine minutes remaining*
Sera Kade came to court wearing the coat she used for night shifts at the river clinic.

Her brother Tomas had been stabbed during a tram robbery. The accused man, Ren Vol, had entered suspension eleven months ago after witnesses identified him. His hearing had been displaced twice by priority petitions.
Sera refused the chair Pell offered.

**Sera Kade**  
If you open him because the pipes are broken, do not call that justice.

**Lysa Ansel**  
If they keep me because his file frightens you, do not call that safety.
The two women faced each other across the hearing table. Neither asked Illuminara to soften the other.

**Sera Kade**  
I am not asking them to keep you.

**Lysa Ansel**  
I know. I am asking them to hear you without making your brother the lock on every door.
Sera's shoulders lowered by less than an inch.

Pell projected Ren Vol's file. The identification was strong. A recovered knife carried Tomas's blood and Vol's skin cells. A second witness had withdrawn testimony after threats. A current assessment named a credible risk to that witness.

**Varo Pell**  
This is what mass release ignores.

**Illuminara**  
Yes.
Pell had prepared for disagreement. Agreement left him momentarily defenseless.

**Illuminara**  
Vol needs an immediate hearing and witness protection. Lysa's case should be dismissed. Everyone else must be governed by their own evidence.

**Sera Kade**  
And if the court cannot hear all of them tonight?

**Nemi Daro**  
Thirty-eight mixed panels: judge, defense advocate, public-risk advocate. The two hundred forty complete files can test the method first.

**Sera Kade**  
Who speaks for a victim when there is no family awake at two in the morning?

**Nemi Daro**  
A panel can impose temporary protection. It cannot invent danger in an absent victim's name.
Sera read the proposed form. She crossed out the phrase presumed community consent.

**Sera Kade**  
No one gets to presume my consent because I could not arrive fast enough.

**Lysa Ansel**  
And no one gets to presume my danger because you could.
Sera looked at her for a long moment.

**Sera Kade**  
Then write both.
Nemi did.
The new review sheet began with two questions: What current evidence justifies restraint? What time has this person already lost while untried?

**Sera Kade**  
Tomas cannot get his eleven months back either.

**Illuminara**  
His safety and his lost time belong in the same room. Neither cancels the other.
Below them, a cooling alarm began to sound.
Pell closed Ren Vol's file.

**Varo Pell**  
The working ledger contains the original witness-protection order. It was never transferred to the public file.
He removed the cabinet key from his pocket.

scenes.title: The Key He Could Keep
paragraphs: *Sealed scheduling office · 03:04, six hours thirteen minutes remaining*
Pell held the key above the lock.

**Varo Pell**  
If I open this, the city will say the vault was evil from its first day. They will tear it out and put the next accused child back in a cage.

**Illuminara**  
That is possible.

**Varo Pell**  
You could take the key.

**Illuminara**  
I could.
Her power could have lifted it without touching his hand. It could not make the act his.

**Varo Pell**  
Why don't you?

**Illuminara**  
Because you built the vault after watching innocent people suffer before trial. That truth is part of the record. So is every hearing you sold. I will not protect your office from consequence, and I will not let the city erase the good you were trying to preserve merely because admitting it makes judgment harder.
Pell looked older than he had on the bridge.

**Varo Pell**  
You offer me understanding as evidence for the prosecution.

**Illuminara**  
I offer it as the reason you still have a useful choice.
She placed a second chair beside Nemi's desk.

**Illuminara**  
Open the ledger. Sit with the first panel under public witness. Restore the continuances you hid. You may defend each decision, but not own the calendar.

**Illuminara**  
My work below will enter the same public record. No one here becomes the part nobody may question.

**Varo Pell**  
And if I refuse?

**Illuminara**  
The record exists. Nemi holds the paper, and the panels will convene either way. Read Lysa's seven continuances aloud, if you choose.
Pell opened the public ledger. He read each cancelled date and the official initials beneath it. At the fourth, his voice roughened. At the seventh, Lysa stopped him.

**Lysa Ansel**  
I know the dates. Do you know why you kept the other record?

**Varo Pell**  
So the lie would not be the only version left.
He turned the key.
The cabinet held ordinary grey folders, each tagged with a bought morning and a displaced name.
Pell took out the first three stacks.

**Varo Pell**  
Red means current danger. Blue is ready for dismissal or release. White needs a factual hearing. The lower mark names who bought the displacement.
Nemi stared at the system she had only seen from outside.

**Nemi Daro**  
You indexed the theft.

**Varo Pell**  
I told myself I was preserving a way back.
Lysa stood in the doorway. She had called her son and heard his adult voice. Whatever had passed between them remained hers.

**Lysa Ansel**  
A way back for whom?
Pell did not ask forgiveness.

**Varo Pell**  
For the institution. Not for you.
He carried the blue files toward Hearing Room One.

**Varo Pell**  
Your dismissal first. Vol's hearing second. Then the oldest complete file unless current danger gives a public reason.

**Lysa Ansel**  
My dismissal is not payment for helping.

**Varo Pell**  
No. It was owed twelve years ago.
Lysa followed him, not beside him.

scenes.title: Thirty-Eight Tables
paragraphs: *Central Court and temporal vault · 04:10, five hours seven minutes remaining*
The court woke before the city.
Thirty-eight tables filled the court. Advocates arrived carrying shoes and files. Judges named in Pell's ledger left the panels; Nemi published their displacement codes.

**Panel Chair**  
My initials are on two displaced files. I cannot sit this table.
Nemi replaced the chair and divided that table's routine files among the other thirty-seven. The public board recorded the delay.
Illuminara moved between two kinds of work.
Below, Illuminara held the trunks while Ishan and six technicians joined the fountain loop to the temporal coils. She marked turbulent joints for them to rebuild rather than hiding them with force.
Above, Illuminara matched Pell's hidden codes to public evidence, exposing duplicated identities, stale risks and missing orders. Human beings questioned them and signed every choice.

At the first two tables, twelve disputed reviews took fifty-three minutes. Around them, ten routine blue-tab orders cleared in under three minutes each; hard cases moved to longer hearings while those tables kept working.
Lysa's charge was dismissed. Seven people received release with stated conditions. Two delayed awakening until support arrived. Ren Vol entered a guarded hearing room awake and represented.

**Ren Vol**  
The knife was mine. Tomas took it from my stall during the fight. I ran because the witness who named me threatened my mother.

The claim did not erase the blood evidence or Sera's fear. It forced the panel to protect both the witness and Vol's mother, preserve the disputed account and set a trial instead of treating suspension as a verdict.
Sera sat behind the public-risk advocate, watching the court stop using unconsciousness as mercy.
At Table Fourteen, another blue-tab file failed because its interpreter order had never transferred.

**Defendant at Table Fourteen**  
I will not wake into a language I cannot understand. Bring the interpreter and my insulin, then ask again.
The panel honoured the refusal. Finding the missing order cost twelve minutes; four neighbouring tables absorbed its routine files while Nemi summoned both supports.
Panels read current evidence, elapsed suspension and the least restraint answering real risk. The board showed counts, delays and the oldest unheard case.
At 05:22, Ishan opened the bypass.
Water struck the first coil too fast. Blue light rippled through Gallery Eight, and forty chambers began returning one thousandth of a second out of phase.

**Ishan Rho, on comms**  
Close it!
Illuminara could have forced every field into alignment. The correction would have passed through the sleeping minds as an unchosen temporal shock.
Instead she held the incoming water motionless for three heartbeats.

**Illuminara**  
The west elbow is feeding a standing wave. Rotate it eleven degrees and shorten the brace by two fingers.
Ishan cut the brace. A technician turned the elbow. Illuminara released one tenth of the flow.
The chambers steadied.

**Ishan Rho**  
Again.
They increased the flow in measured steps until ordinary water carried the heat that extraordinary force had only held.

**Ishan Rho**  
The fountain loop can carry loaded coils until ten. Empty chambers can transfer to reserve power. We have one morning to move every person through an order.
At the thirty-eighth table, Pell named each purchased petition in a file he had displaced four times.

**Varo Pell**  
Release with a location condition. Review compensation now. My continuances caused eleven years and three months.
The panel chair asked whether Pell wished to recuse himself.

**Varo Pell**  
I am not deciding. I am accounting.
On the public board, cleared blue-tab files began climbing by the minute while disputed stacks moved sideways into lit hearing rooms.

scenes.title: A Morning No One Could Buy
paragraphs: *Central Court steps · 09:41, after sunrise*
No one died in the vault.

Two thousand nine hundred forty-one defendants had been awakened and released, most without custody. Five hundred thirty-seven returned only when family, housing, medication or an interpreter stood ready. Three hundred twenty-two high-risk cases moved to immediate hearings with representation, witness protection and a twenty-four-hour deadline.
Suspension remained available only by a person's informed request during that deadline. The brass hearing seal no longer belonged to one magistrate.
Pell left the court through the same doors as everyone else. Two civic investigators walked with him, not guards from the temporal vault. His preliminary hearing was set for noon.

Before he went, he signed an order preserving the machine and ending the market: oldest unheard case first, public urgency, no purchased priority, every continuance visible to the person whose time it used.
The order did not absolve him. It kept the city from discarding the mercy corruption had occupied.
Lysa stood on the steps in a borrowed coat. Her son waited across the square.
He was taller than she was. She recognized the way he held one shoulder before she recognized his face.
For a moment neither moved. The city had prepared speeches for reunions like this. None of them crossed the square.
Lysa walked first.
Her son met her halfway.
Sera emerged behind Illuminara. She had stayed until Ren Vol's hearing produced a protection order and a trial date that could not be displaced by money.

**Sera Kade**  
I still think some of them should have remained held.

**Illuminara**  
You may be right about particular people.

**Sera Kade**  
That is less comforting than I expected.

**Illuminara**  
It keeps the question where an answer can reach it.
On the public board above the court doors, the number of sleeping defendants fell to zero. Beneath it, a new line appeared: TIME ALREADY TAKEN. The total was measured in years.
Nemi had refused to let the city round it down.
Pell stopped before the board.

**Varo Pell**  
I thought painless time was empty.
Lysa had reached her son. She heard Pell and turned without leaving the young man's arms.

**Lysa Ansel**  
It was full. You were simply not inside it.
Pell accepted the words without making acceptance another claim on her.
He went to his hearing.

The first ordinary case of the morning was called at 09:47. No contribution preceded it. No hidden code moved it. The clerk spoke the defendant's name, the victim's name and the time both had already waited.
Illuminara remained until the answer began.

critic_line: A chief magistrate sold the court's mornings to the rich and left 3,800 poor defendants asleep for years; when the vault failed, Illuminara held the pipes steady while the people she had woken, and the man who built the machine, decided what justice would cost.

shared_strengths: Strong high-concept premise, humane tone, dialogue-heavy, and the Lysa reunion is affecting. Held back by tidy, speechifying resolution, procedural and abstract middle sections, and a too-agreeable antagonist. Readers who like idea-driven speculative fiction will likely finish, but it is only moderately sticky.

A morally complex premise, humane reversals, vivid dialogue, and emotionally earned resolution strongly fit these readers. Lysa, Sera, and Pell prevent the dilemma from becoming simplistic. The procedural final third and occasional thesis-like dialogue may feel over-explained, but the lost-time metaphor and reunion should remain memorable.
shared_reservations: Pell had built the first chambers after three innocent people died in a fevered remand block. Every later compromise had entered through that memory wearing the face of rescue.
At the first two tables, twelve disputed reviews took fifty-three minutes.

translation_sl.title: SODNIK, KI JE PRODAL JUTRI
translation_sl.deck: Vrhovni sodnik Varo Pell je zgradil neboleč časovni trezor, da noben človek pred sojenjem ne bi zavestno preživel niti dneva v zaporu. Nato je sodna jutra prodal premožnim in 3.800 revnih obtožencev pustil v suspenziji, medtem ko so zunaj minevala leta. Ko okvara hlajenja trezorju pusti devet ur, mora Illuminara rešiti vsako življenje, ne da bi množično izpustitev spremenila v še en način, kako preslišati ogrožene ljudi.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov v devetih urah: okvarjajoči se časovni trezor pod sodiščem; prebujenje ženske, katere primer je čakal najdlje; odkritje plačanega razporeda obravnav, skritega v humanem stroju; žrtev, ki zavrne tako splošno izpustitev kot neskončno suspenzijo; Pellova odločitev, da odpre knjigo, ki ga lahko razkrije; osemintrideset javnih revizijskih miz, ki delujejo, medtem ko Illuminara in inženirji stabilizirajo trezor; in zora, v kateri nihče ne umre, večina obtožencev znova dobi sorazmerno svobodo, nevarni primeri so resnično obravnavani, mož, ki je prodal jutri, pa začne polagati račune za čas, ki ga je vzel.

scenes.title: Devet ur pod sodiščem
paragraphs: *Osrednje sodišče v Lyru, časovni trezor · 00:17, preostaja devet ur*
Prvi znak okvare ni bil alarm. Bil je dež.

Na bakrenih rebrih časovnega trezorja se je nabirala hladna voda in v počasnih, bleščečih kapljah padala skozi modro svetlobo. Vsaka kaplja je prečkala polje suspenzije in postala vrsta drobnih krogel, devet različic iste vode, ki so zasedale devet sosednjih trenutkov.
Pod sodiščem se je v dvanajstih krožnih galerijah spuščalo tri tisoč osemsto steklenih komor. V vsaki je počival človek, brez bolečin in staranja, medtem ko je mesto nadaljevalo brez njega.

Illuminara je stala na osrednjem mostu z eno roko ob hladilnem vodu. Kovina je za steno počila. Čutila je, kako se razpoka veji proti še trem vodom in kako vroče časovne tuljave vlečejo proti običajnemu času.
Inženir trezorja Ishan Rho je klečal ob odprti servisni plošči. Rokavice so se mu kadile tam, kjer je menjal ventil.

**Ishan Rho**  
Rezervni krog nam da devet ur, če ne poči nič drugega. Če se jedro segreje nad enajst stopinj, bo vsaka komora svojega človeka vrnila v drugem delčku sekunde.

**Illuminara**  
Živega?
Rho je pogledal skozi dvanajst galerij spečih obrazov.

**Ishan Rho**  
Nekatere. Drugi bi prispeli v kosih časa.

Vrhovni sodnik Varo Pell je brez plašča prišel čez most. Imel je šestdeset let, bil urejen celo ob polnoči in nosil medeninast pečat obravnave, s katerim je bilo mogoče po zakonitem nalogu odpreti katerokoli komoro.

**Varo Pell**  
Nobena komora se ne odpre brez revizije.

**Illuminara**  
Potem začnite revizije.

**Varo Pell**  
Tri tisoč osemsto jih je.

**Illuminara**  
Devet ur je.
Pell je opazoval suspendiranega moškega, čigar roke so bile zvite, kakor da še vedno držijo ograjo, s katere so ga odpeljali sodni stražarji.

**Varo Pell**  
Pred tem trezorjem so ljudi pred sojenjem pretepali, okužili in novačili še pred vsako sodbo. Tukaj ne čutijo mrzlega jutra ali prestrašene noči.

**Illuminara**  
In nobenega rojstnega dne.
Pogled se mu je izostril, vendar ni pogledal stran.

**Varo Pell**  
Odprite vse komore in nekateri od teh ljudi bodo ubijali pred zajtrkom. Njihova leta boste rešili tako, da boste porabili življenje nekoga drugega.
Ugovor ni bil izgovor. Zato je bil izgovor okoli njega še nevarnejši.
Illuminara je sledila razpoki skozi ritem hlajenja. Kovino je lahko držala, toda noben dotik ni mogel sprejeti sodne odločitve.

**Illuminara**  
Rhoju lahko ohranjam stabilen tlak, medtem ko gradi obvod. To varuje možnost odločanja. Ne odloča namesto nas.

**Illuminara**  
Ljudje znotraj. Ljudje, ki bi bili zunaj lahko ogroženi. Uradniki, ki vedo, zakaj so se obravnave ustavile. Vi. In prvi človek, ki mu je to sodišče vzelo čas.
Pellovi prsti so se sklenili okoli pečata obravnave.

**Varo Pell**  
Najstarejši primer ni najvarnejši primer.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Je prvi račun, ki smo ga dolžni poravnati.
Druga cev je tiho kovinsko zastokala. Illuminara je pritisnila razpoko skupaj, ne da bi jo zmečkala.
Dež je ponehal. Ura ni.

scenes.title: Prva oseba nazaj
paragraphs: *Časovni trezor, dvanajsta galerija · 00:51, preostaja osem ur in šestindvajset minut*
Najdlje zasedena komora je pripadala Lysi Ansel.

V njenem spisu je pisalo: dvaintrideset let, občinska knjigovodkinja, obtožena preusmeritve zimskih dobropisov za gorivo. Paket dokazov je bil popoln dvanajst let. Sedem datumov obravnave je bilo odpovedanih. Ob zadnji odpovedi je nekdo vnesel kodo, ki je pomenila, da je koledar izrinila prednostna prošnja.
Pell je odprtje dovolil šele, ko je Ishan okoli komore namestil prenosno povratno zibelko.
Modra svetloba se je prepognila navznoter. Lysa je vdihnila zadnji dih zimskega popoldneva in izdihnila v poletno polnoč dvanajst let pozneje.
Najprej si je rokave potegnila čez roke. Nato je poiskala okno.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Sodna dvorana?

**Illuminara**  
Pod njo. Varni ste. Vaše telo je od prijetja doživelo manj kot minuto.
Lysa je preučila Illuminari obraz, nato Pellov pečat.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Koliko zamujajo?
Pell je začel odgovarjati. Illuminara je dvignila prst, ne da bi ga utišala, temveč da njegov urad ne bi posedoval prvega dejstva.

**Illuminara**  
Minilo je dvanajst let, osem mesecev in štiri dni.
Lysa ni zajela sape. Njeno telo se še ni naučilo dovolj novega prostora, da bi lahko odigralo žalost.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Moj sin je bil star šest let.

**Varo Pell**  
Vaša družina je bila obveščena o vsaki preložitvi.
Lysa ga je pogledala, kakor da je odgovoril na drugo vprašanje.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Je bil star šest let, ko jih je bral?
Nihče ni spregovoril.
Illuminara je poznala javne evidence, vendar so ta dejstva pripadala Lysi, in ne vsa naenkrat.

**Illuminara**  
Živ je. Star je osemnajst let. Želite njegovo sedanje ime in stik ali želite, da vam pove nekdo, ki ga poznate?
Lysa je obe dlani pritisnila ob povratno zibelko.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Sedanje ime?

**Illuminara**  
Uporablja Ansel. Obdržal je vašega.
Prva solza je prišla, preden se je Lysin obraz spremenil.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Potem mi povejte, zakaj sem še vedno obtožena.
Distributer je uporabil Lysin ključ, medtem ko so jo kamere postavljale drugam. Njegov lastnik je priznal pred enajstimi leti; noben tožilec ni nasprotoval zavrženju.

**Varo Pell**  
To bi moralo biti zaključeno.

**Lysa Ansel**  
»Bi moralo« je soba brez vrat.
Dotaknila se je stekla, ki jo je držalo.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Koliko?

**Illuminara**  
Tri tisoč osemsto komor. Dvesto štirideset spisov je označenih kot pripravljenih za takojšnjo revizijo. Menimo, da jih veliko več vsebuje dovolj dokazov za varno odločitev.

**Lysa Ansel**  
In hlajenje?

**Ishan Rho**  
Zdaj osem ur.
Ko je Lysa vstala, so se ji tresle noge. Illuminara ji je ponudila podlaket. Lysa jo je prijela, ne zato, ker bi zaupala sodišču, temveč zato, ker so tla brez njenega dovoljenja dobila dvanajst let.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Ne naredite iz mene zgodbe, ki dokazuje, da so vsi neškodljivi.

**Illuminara**  
Ne bom.

**Lysa Ansel**  
In ne uporabite enega nevarnega spisa, da bi me vrnili nazaj.

**Illuminara**  
Tudi tega ne bom storila.
Lysa je enkrat pokimala.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Potem mi pokažite koledar, ki je odločil, da lahko moj sin odraste prvi.

scenes.title: Tržnica jutra
paragraphs: *Osrednje sodišče, zapečateni urad za razporejanje · 01:39, preostaja sedem ur in osemintrideset minut*
Višja uradnica Nemi Daro je tri leta spala v uradu za razporejanje.
Med policami papirnatih preložitev je stala ozka postelja. Nemi je dejala, da je digitalni koledar mogoče spreminjati, papir pa si še vedno zapomni pritisk.
Na mizo je položila dve knjigi. V javni knjigi so bili datumi obravnav. V zasebni pa prispevki v Sklad časovne milosti.

**Nemi Daro**  
Družine, ki so financirale širitev, so sprva za vsako komoro dobile eno prednostno obravnavo. Kmalu je bogastvo kupilo torek, še preden je revščina dosegla ponedeljek.
Lysa je obračala strani. Vsaka zlata oznaka je predstavljala prejeti denar. Vsaka črna oznaka prestavljeno obravnavo.

Illuminara je javni koledar položila ob zasebno knjigo. Za vse druge oči so bile črne oznake odpovedi. Zanjo so bile ritem: stotine so se zgostile v oseminštiridesetih urah pred četrtletnimi poročili Sklada milosti.
Iste tri začetnice v spodnjem kotu so se ponavljale. Primeri so se premaknili tik preden je svet dohodek od pristojbin štel kot dokaz, da se trezor lahko financira sam.

**Illuminara**  
Tržnica ni zgolj kupovala juter. Revni obtoženci so morali ostati spodaj, da je bil sklad videti nepogrešljiv.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Sedem črnih oznak ob mojem imenu.

**Varo Pell**  
Pristojbine so zgradile dva tisoč šeststo komor. Sicer bi tisoči ostali v zaporu.

**Nemi Daro**  
Stari zapor so zaprli v četrtem letu.

**Varo Pell**  
Zakladnica pa je v petem letu zavrnila polno financiranje.
Pell je prve komore zgradil potem, ko so v vročičnem pripornem bloku umrli trije nedolžni ljudje. Vsak poznejši kompromis je vstopil skozi ta spomin z obrazom rešitve.
Nemi je odprla prilogo o vzdrževanju. Šest let so prednostni prispevki presegali stroške trezorja. Presežek je financiral novo sodno krilo in znižal pravosodno dajatev.

**Varo Pell**  
Končajte prošnje in svet bo vzel presežek ter oklestil trezor. Neboleč pripor jim je bil všeč, ker ga je plačal nekdo drug.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Nekdo drug ga je res plačal.
Dlan je položila na zasebno knjigo.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Plačali smo ga s časom, za katerega niste mogli videti, da ga čutimo.
Skozi tla je šel sunek. Daleč spodaj se je Illuminarino polje upognilo okoli hladilnega voda.

**Ishan Rho, po zvezi**  
Razpoka je dosegla četrti vod. Lahko ga osamim, vendar so stari načrti obvoda napačni.
Pell je pogledal proti zaklenjeni omari za svojo mizo.
Illuminara je opazila.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj je v njej?

**Varo Pell**  
Moja delovna knjiga.

**Nemi Daro**  
Pravi razlogi za preložitve. Katera prošnja je izrinila kateri primer. Kateri spisi so bili pripravljeni. Katera poročila o tveganju so bila veljavna.

**Illuminara**  
Ohranili ste drugi odgovor. Zakaj bi ga hranili, če ste nameravali, da ga javnost nikoli ne sliši?

**Varo Pell**  
Ker bi uničenje knjige laž naredilo dokončno.

**Varo Pell**  
Imenuje vse vpletene uradnike. Odprite jo in polovica ljudi, ki jih potrebujemo za revizije, bo najprej zaščitila sebe.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Pustite jo zaprto in naše ure porabljajo za vašo zaščito.
Pell je medeninasti pečat položil na mizo, ključ omare pa obdržal v žepu.

**Varo Pell**  
Želite si čistega zlikovca, ker je pokvarjen stroj lažje popraviti kot mesto, ki je prosilo za milost, ne da bi plačalo za pravičnost.

**Illuminara**  
Ne mislim, da ste čisti.

**Illuminara**  
Razumevanje, kako ste prispeli sem, ne izbriše kraja, kamor ste prispeli. Preden vas znova prosim za knjigo, bomo slišali osebo, katere nevarnosti se najbolj bojite.
Pellova roka je zapustila ključ, ne pa tudi žepa.

scenes.title: Oseba zunaj komore
paragraphs: *Osrednje sodišče, prva sodna dvorana · 02:28, preostaja šest ur in devetinštirideset minut*
Sera Kade je prišla na sodišče v plašču, ki ga je uporabljala za nočne izmene v kliniki ob reki.

Njenega brata Tomasa so zabodli med ropom tramvaja. Obtoženi Ren Vol je v suspenzijo vstopil pred enajstimi meseci, potem ko so ga prepoznale priče. Njegovo obravnavo sta dvakrat izrinili prednostni prošnji.
Sera je zavrnila stol, ki ji ga je ponudil Pell.

**Sera Kade**  
Če ga odprete, ker so cevi pokvarjene, temu ne recite pravičnost.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Če mene zadržijo, ker vas njegov spis straši, temu ne recite varnost.
Ženski sta si stali nasproti čez mizo za obravnave. Nobena ni prosila Illuminare, naj omili drugo.

**Sera Kade**  
Ne prosim jih, naj vas zadržijo.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Vem. Prosim jih, naj vas slišijo, ne da bi iz vašega brata naredili ključavnico na vseh vratih.
Serina ramena so se spustila za manj kot palec.

Pell je prikazal spis Rena Vola. Prepoznava je bila trdna. Na najdenem nožu sta bili Tomasova kri in Volove kožne celice. Druga priča je po grožnjah umaknila izjavo. Aktualna ocena je navajala verodostojno tveganje za to pričo.

**Varo Pell**  
To množična izpustitev spregleda.

**Illuminara**  
Da.
Pell se je pripravil na nestrinjanje. Strinjanje ga je za trenutek pustilo brez obrambe.

**Illuminara**  
Vol potrebuje takojšnjo obravnavo in zaščito prič. Lysin primer je treba zavreči. Vsi drugi morajo biti presojani po lastnih dokazih.

**Sera Kade**  
Kaj pa, če sodišče nocoj ne more obravnavati vseh?

**Nemi Daro**  
Osemintrideset mešanih senatov: sodnik, zagovornik, zagovornik javne varnosti. Najprej lahko metodo preizkusi dvesto štirideset popolnih spisov.

**Sera Kade**  
Kdo govori za žrtev, ko ob dveh zjutraj ni buden nihče iz družine?

**Nemi Daro**  
Senat lahko odredi začasno zaščito. Ne more si izmisliti nevarnosti v imenu odsotne žrtve.
Sera je prebrala predlagani obrazec. Prečrtala je besede domnevno soglasje skupnosti.

**Sera Kade**  
Nihče ne sme domnevati mojega soglasja, ker nisem mogla priti dovolj hitro.

**Lysa Ansel**  
In nihče ne sme domnevati moje nevarnosti, ker vi ste.
Sera jo je dolgo gledala.

**Sera Kade**  
Potem napišite oboje.
Nemi je.
Novi obrazec za revizijo se je začel z dvema vprašanjema: Kateri trenutni dokazi upravičujejo omejitev? Koliko časa je ta človek že izgubil brez sojenja?

**Sera Kade**  
Tudi Tomas svojih enajstih mesecev ne more dobiti nazaj.

**Illuminara**  
Njegova varnost in njegov izgubljeni čas sodita v isti prostor. Eno ne razveljavi drugega.
Pod njimi se je oglasil alarm hlajenja.
Pell je zaprl spis Rena Vola.

**Varo Pell**  
V delovni knjigi je izvirni nalog za zaščito priče. Nikoli ni bil prenesen v javni spis.
Iz žepa je vzel ključ omare.

scenes.title: Ključ, ki ga je lahko obdržal
paragraphs: *Zapečateni urad za razporejanje · 03:04, preostaja šest ur in trinajst minut*
Pell je držal ključ nad ključavnico.

**Varo Pell**  
Če jo odprem, bo mesto reklo, da je bil trezor zloben od prvega dne. Raztrgali ga bodo in naslednjega obtoženega otroka vrnili v kletko.

**Illuminara**  
To je mogoče.

**Varo Pell**  
Lahko bi vzeli ključ.

**Illuminara**  
Lahko bi ga.
Njena moč bi ga lahko dvignila, ne da bi se dotaknila njegove roke. Ni mogla dejanja narediti njegovega.

**Varo Pell**  
Zakaj ga ne?

**Illuminara**  
Ker ste trezor zgradili, potem ko ste gledali nedolžne ljudi trpeti pred sojenjem. Ta resnica je del evidence. Prav tako vsaka obravnava, ki ste jo prodali. Vašega urada ne bom zaščitila pred posledicami in mestu ne bom dovolila izbrisati dobrega, ki ste ga skušali ohraniti, zgolj zato, ker priznanje oteži presojo.
Pell je bil videti starejši kakor na mostu.

**Varo Pell**  
Razumevanje mi ponujate kot dokaz za tožilstvo.

**Illuminara**  
Ponujam ga kot razlog, da imate še vedno koristno izbiro.
Ob Nemijino mizo je postavila drugi stol.

**Illuminara**  
Odprite knjigo. Sedite s prvim senatom pod javnim nadzorom. Obnovite preložitve, ki ste jih skrili. Vsako odločitev lahko zagovarjate, ne morete pa si lastiti koledarja.

**Illuminara**  
Moje delo spodaj bo vstopilo v isto javno evidenco. Nihče tukaj ne postane del, ki ga nihče ne sme vprašati.

**Varo Pell**  
Kaj pa, če zavrnem?

**Illuminara**  
Evidenca obstaja. Nemi ima papir, senati pa se bodo sestali v vsakem primeru. Če želite, na glas preberite Lysinih sedem preložitev.
Pell je odprl javno knjigo. Prebral je vsak odpovedani datum in uradne začetnice pod njim. Pri četrtem mu je glas postal hrapav. Pri sedmem ga je Lysa ustavila.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Datume poznam. Ali veste, zakaj ste obdržali drugo evidenco?

**Varo Pell**  
Da laž ne bi bila edina preostala različica.
Obrnil je ključ.
V omari so bile običajne sive mape, vsaka označena s kupljenim jutrom in izrinjenim imenom.
Pell je vzel prve tri kupe.

**Varo Pell**  
Rdeča pomeni trenutno nevarnost. Modra je pripravljena za zavrženje ali izpustitev. Bela potrebuje dokazno obravnavo. Spodnja oznaka pove, kdo je kupil izrinitev.
Nemi je strmela v sistem, ki ga je dotlej videla le od zunaj.

**Nemi Daro**  
Tatvino ste indeksirali.

**Varo Pell**  
Govoril sem si, da ohranjam pot nazaj.
Lysa je stala v vratih. Poklicala je sina in slišala njegov odrasli glas. Karkoli je šlo med njima, je ostalo njuno.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Pot nazaj za koga?
Pell ni prosil odpuščanja.

**Varo Pell**  
Za ustanovo. Ne za vas.
Modre spise je odnesel proti prvi sodni dvorani.

**Varo Pell**  
Najprej vaša zavržba. Volova obravnava druga. Nato najstarejši popoln spis, razen če trenutna nevarnost ne da javnega razloga.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Zavržba mojega primera ni plačilo za pomoč.

**Varo Pell**  
Ne. Dolgovali smo jo pred dvanajstimi leti.
Lysa mu je sledila, ne ob njem.

scenes.title: Osemintrideset miz
paragraphs: *Osrednje sodišče in časovni trezor · 04:10, preostaja pet ur in sedem minut*
Sodišče se je zbudilo pred mestom.
Sodišče je napolnilo osemintrideset miz. Zagovorniki so prihajali s čevlji in spisi. Sodniki, imenovani v Pellovi knjigi, so zapustili senate; Nemi je objavila njihove kode izrinitev.

**Predsedujoči senata**  
Moje začetnice so na dveh izrinjenih spisih. Pri tej mizi ne morem sedeti.
Nemi je zamenjala predsedujočega in rutinske spise te mize razdelila med preostalih sedemintrideset. Javna tabla je zabeležila zamudo.
Illuminara se je premikala med dvema vrstama dela.
Spodaj je držala vode, medtem ko so Ishan in šest tehnikov povezovali krog vodnjaka s časovnimi tuljavami. Označila jim je turbulentne spoje, da so jih obnovili, namesto da bi jih prikrila s silo.
Zgoraj je Pellove skrite kode povezovala z javnimi dokazi ter razkrivala podvojene identitete, zastarela tveganja in manjkajoče naloge. Ljudje so jih izprašali in podpisali vsako odločitev.

Pri prvih dveh mizah je dvanajst spornih revizij trajalo triinpetdeset minut. Okoli njiju je bilo deset rutinskih nalogov z modro oznako rešenih v manj kot treh minutah vsak; težki primeri so šli v daljše obravnave, medtem ko sta mizi nadaljevali delo.

Obtožbo proti Lysi so zavrgli. Sedem ljudi je dobilo izpustitev z navedenimi pogoji. Dva sta prebujenje odložila, dokler ni prispela podpora. Ren Vol je buden in z zastopnikom vstopil v varovano sodno dvorano.

**Ren Vol**  
Nož je bil moj. Tomas ga je med pretepom vzel z moje stojnice. Pobegnil sem, ker je priča, ki me je imenovala, grozila moji materi.

Trditev ni izbrisala krvnih dokazov ali Serinega strahu. Senat je prisilila, da zaščiti tako pričo kot Volovo mater, ohrani sporni opis in določi sojenje, namesto da bi suspenzijo obravnaval kot sodbo.
Sera je sedela za zagovornikom javne varnosti in opazovala, kako sodišče nezavest preneha uporabljati kot milost.
Pri štirinajsti mizi je drug spis z modro oznako padel, ker nalog za tolmača ni bil nikoli prenesen.

**Obtoženec pri štirinajsti mizi**  
Ne bom se zbudil v jezik, ki ga ne razumem. Pripeljite tolmača in moj inzulin, potem vprašajte znova.
Senat je zavrnitev spoštoval. Iskanje manjkajočega naloga je vzelo dvanajst minut; štiri sosednje mize so prevzele rutinske spise, medtem ko je Nemi poklicala obe podpori.
Senati so brali trenutne dokaze, pretečeni čas v suspenziji in najmanjšo omejitev, ki je odgovarjala na resnično tveganje. Tabla je kazala število, zamude in najstarejši še neslišani primer.
Ob 05:22 je Ishan odprl obvod.
Voda je v prvo tuljavo udarila prehitro. Modra svetloba je zavalovala skozi osmo galerijo in štirideset komor se je začelo vračati za tisočinko sekunde iz faze.

**Ishan Rho, po zvezi**  
Zapri ga!
Illuminara bi lahko vsa polja prisilila v poravnavo. Popravek bi skozi speče ume prešel kot neizbran časovni šok.
Namesto tega je dotekajočo vodo za tri utripe srca zadržala negibno.

**Illuminara**  
Zahodni komolec napaja stoječi val. Zavrtite ga za enajst stopinj in oporo skrajšajte za dva prsta.
Ishan je odrezal oporo. Tehnik je zavrtel komolec. Illuminara je sprostila desetino pretoka.
Komore so se umirile.

**Ishan Rho**  
Znova.
Pretok so povečevali v odmerjenih korakih, dokler ni navadna voda odvajala toplote, ki jo je izjemna sila dotlej le zadrževala.

**Ishan Rho**  
Krog vodnjaka lahko do desete ure nosi obremenjene tuljave. Prazne komore lahko prenesemo na rezervno napajanje. Eno jutro imamo, da vsakega človeka spravimo skozi nalog.
Pri osemintrideseti mizi je Pell imenoval vsako kupljeno prošnjo v spisu, ki ga je štirikrat izrinil.

**Varo Pell**  
Izpustitev s pogojem kraja bivanja. Odškodnino preglejte zdaj. Moje preložitve so povzročile enajst let in tri mesece.
Predsedujoči senata je vprašal, ali se želi Pell izločiti.

**Varo Pell**  
Ne odločam. Polagam račune.
Na javni tabli so se rešeni spisi z modro oznako začeli iz minute v minuto vzpenjati, sporni kupi pa so se pomikali vstran, v osvetljene sodne dvorane.

scenes.title: Jutro, ki ga nihče ni mogel kupiti
paragraphs: *Stopnice Osrednjega sodišča · 09:41, po sončnem vzhodu*
V trezorju ni umrl nihče.

Prebudili in izpustili so dva tisoč devetsto enainštirideset obtožencev, večino brez pripora. Petsto sedemintrideset se jih je vrnilo šele, ko so bili pripravljeni družina, stanovanje, zdravila ali tolmač. Tristo dvaindvajset primerov z visokim tveganjem je šlo v takojšnje obravnave z zastopanjem, zaščito prič in štiriindvajseturnim rokom.
Suspenzija je med tem rokom ostala na voljo le na podlagi človekove obveščene zahteve. Medeninasti pečat obravnave ni več pripadal enemu sodniku.
Pell je sodišče zapustil skozi ista vrata kakor vsi drugi. Z njim sta hodila dva državljanska preiskovalca, ne stražarja iz časovnega trezorja. Njegova predhodna obravnava je bila določena za poldne.

Pred odhodom je podpisal nalog, ki je ohranil stroj in končal tržnico: najprej najstarejši neslišani primer, javna nujnost, brez kupljene prednosti, vsaka preložitev vidna človeku, čigar čas porablja.
Nalog ga ni oprostil. Mestu je preprečil, da zavrže milost, ki jo je zasedla korupcija.
Lysa je stala na stopnicah v izposojenem plašču. Njen sin je čakal čez trg.
Bil je višji od nje. Način, kako je držal eno ramo, je prepoznala, preden je prepoznala njegov obraz.
Za trenutek se nobeden ni premaknil. Mesto je za takšna snidenja pripravilo govore. Nobeden ni prečkal trga.
Lysa je stopila prva.
Sin ji je prišel naproti na pol poti.
Za Illuminaro je prišla Sera. Ostala je, dokler obravnava Rena Vola ni prinesla zaščitnega naloga in datuma sojenja, ki ga denar ni mogel izriniti.

**Sera Kade**  
Še vedno mislim, da bi morali nekateri ostati pridržani.

**Illuminara**  
Pri posameznih ljudeh imate morda prav.

**Sera Kade**  
To je manj tolažilno, kot sem pričakovala.

**Illuminara**  
Vprašanje ohranja tam, kjer ga odgovor lahko doseže.
Na javni tabli nad sodnimi vrati je število spečih obtožencev padlo na nič. Pod njim se je pojavila nova vrstica: ČAS, KI JE ŽE BIL VZET. Skupna vrednost je bila merjena v letih.
Nemi mestu ni dovolila, da jo zaokroži navzdol.
Pell se je ustavil pred tablo.

**Varo Pell**  
Mislil sem, da je neboleč čas prazen.
Lysa je dosegla sina. Slišala je Pella in se obrnila, ne da bi zapustila mladeničev objem.

**Lysa Ansel**  
Bil je poln. Le vi niste bili v njem.
Pell je besede sprejel, ne da bi iz sprejetja naredil še eno zahtevo do nje.
Odšel je na svojo obravnavo.
Prvi običajni primer jutra so poklicali ob 09:47. Pred njim ni bilo prispevka. Nobena skrita koda ga ni premaknila. Uradnik je izgovoril ime obtoženca, ime žrtve in čas, ki sta ga oba že čakala.
Illuminara je ostala, dokler se odgovor ni začel.

translation_sl.critic_line: Vrhovni sodnik je bogatim prodal sodna jutra in 3.800 revnih obtožencev pustil leta spati; ko je trezor odpovedal, je Illuminara držala cevi pri miru, medtem ko so ljudje, ki jih je prebudila, in mož, ki je zgradil stroj, odločali, koliko bo stala pravičnost.
